unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 6: LIFE IN THE WORLD & CULTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''Life in the World and Culture'' with a focus on cultural celebrations and sports cultures and competitions. Students will research and compare significant cultural celebrations from around the world, such as music festivals, art exhibitions, and traditional holidays, exploring their historical origins, meanings, and global impact. They will also examine sports cultures, highlighting the importance of various sports in different countries and regions, and analyse major sports competitions, such as the Olympics. The assignment will include a presentation that contrasts cultural celebrations and sports events, showing how they reflect the values and traditions of different societies. Students will also discuss how these celebrations and sports competitions promote cultural exchange, unity, and global understanding. Finally, they will reflect on how participating in or observing such events contributes to shaping identities and fostering a sense of community. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the world and culture with its components such as cultural (music and art) celebrations in the world; sports and sports cultures and competitions'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 11 may know what life in the world and culture, cultural (music and art) celebrations in the world; sports and sports cultures and competitions mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the world and culture'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''match, to win, to lose, traditional, festival'' and also some structures such as ''He is the footballer who won the fair play medal. This international festival which is held in the city hosts thousands of people from different countries'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''cultural (music and art) celebrations in the world; sports and sports cultures and competitions'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about cultural celebrations in the world, sports and sports cultures and competitions in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Global Music and Sports Highlights The teacher starts by showing clips of famous music festivals (e.g., Salzburg Festival, Glastonbury) and sports competitions (e.g., FIFA World Cup, Wimbledon) and asks students to discuss where they take place and what makes them special. The teacher introduces target vocabulary such as ''orchestra'', ''anthem'', ''athlete'', ''stadium'', and ''championship'' with example sentences using defining and non-defining relative clauses (e.g., ''Wimbledon, which takes place in England, is famous for tennis''). Students then choose one festival or competition, write sentences describing it, and explain why it is important using connecting words such as ''therefore'' or ''thus'' (e.g., ''This event is popular worldwide; therefore, it attracts many visitors''.). Finally, students present their work to the class. The teacher gives feedback on the accuracy of their sentences and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about cultural celebrations in the world; sports and sports cultures and competitions in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Music and Sports Around the World The teacher starts the lesson by showing pictures of famous music festivals and sports events (e.g., FIFA World Cup, Olympics) and asks students if they know them, where they are held, or if they have seen them before. Then, the teacher introduces simple words like ''orchestra'', ''anthem'', ''parade'', ''stadium'', ''athlete'', and ''championship'' with example sentences such as ''Orange Flower Carnival is held in Adana, in Türkiye, and it has colourful parades''. Students pick a music festival or sports event, write one or two sentences about it, and draw a picture. Finally, they show their drawings to the class, explain where the event happens and why they chose it, while the teacher gives feedback on their sentences and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
